# Private PR review drafts: public relay

The workflow in `.github/workflows/pr-review-draft-relay.yml` sends `pr-response-request-v1` events for new inline review comments, submitted reviews with nonempty bodies, and top-level PR comments on open BabylonJS/Babylon.js pull requests authored by GitHub user ID `4152247` (`Popov72`). It does not send reviewer text, call an AI model, modify PR code, or post comments. The separate worker and unpublished proposed replies and patches belong in the **private** `Popov72/pr-response-drafts` repository; do not move its agent workflow or private issues here.

Each dispatch has exactly six `client_payload` fields: numeric `source_repository_id` (`11007313`), `source_owner` (`BabylonJS`), `source_repo` (`Babylon.js`), numeric `pr_number`, `kind` (`review_comment`, `review`, or `issue_comment`), and numeric `event_id` (the comment or review ID). The [worker README](https://github.com/Popov72/pr-response-drafts/blob/popov72-private-pr-draft-worker/README.md) defines the contract. Review bodies without text do not generate a dispatch; inline comments in the same review use their own IDs.

Before merging/enabling the relay:

1. Install and validate the private worker on its default branch. Check its owner access, model billing, notice credential, private-issue storage, and output privacy first.
2. An authorized BabylonJS administrator must configure the Actions secret `PR_REVIEW_DISPATCH_TOKEN` with a **dedicated, narrowly scoped** credential that can call `POST /repos/Popov72/pr-response-drafts/dispatches` (fine-grained PAT: private destination repository **Contents: write**; a GitHub App installation token with equivalent access is also suitable). Do not use a broad OAuth session token or commit the credential. The source workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` can read BabylonJS pull requests but cannot dispatch to another repository.
3. Verify BabylonJS Actions policy permits the workflow, then test an eligible PR review and check the private report and the fixed public notice. GitHub does not run a comment-event workflow until the workflow file is on the default branch.

The relay rejects bot and PR-author comments, as well as comments containing the fixed `<!-- pr-response-notice:` marker even if the notice credential belongs to another regular user. The private worker independently revalidates the source event, author identity, PR head SHA, and notice state. Fork PR code must be treated as untrusted data, never executed in a privileged job. Missing credentials fail eligible events explicitly instead of producing a success-shaped result. Avoid posting draft replies, creating pending reviews, or changing the PR branch before the author manually approves and applies a proposal.

The destination worker stores an unpublished report in a private issue and posts only a fixed availability notice after storing it. A public reader cannot open the private issue; the PR author must inspect and manually apply any proposed response or patch. Do not merge this draft relay or send a live dispatch until the worker, scoped credentials, organization policy, and model entitlement have been checked.

References: [GitHub Actions review/comment events](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows), [repository dispatch permissions](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/repos#create-a-repository-dispatch-event).
